newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty flat, foreigners cool about '97 crawl cut.
newsitem.headline: Zloty flat, foreigners cool about '97 crawl cut.

text.p: The Polish zloty held flat against the basket of currencies in thin early trade as economic and political events from Thursday had little immediate impact on financial markets, dealers said.

They said the zloty would likely follow dollar/mark swings in the absence of vivifying foreign orders on Friday, even after the central bank singalled that it could cut the zloty's crawling peg devaluation factor next year.
"Markets had no immediate reaction to yesterday's central bank policy outline for zloty devaluation in 1997," said Wojciech Kowalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA.
At the 0910 GMT the zloty was at 1.81/1.76 percent from the trading band centre against opening's 1.83/1.76 percent and 1.78/1.75 percent on Thursday.
It was at 2.8230/48 to the dollar flat from 2.8225/45 at 0700 GMT and at 1.8543/48 to the mark against 1.8535/55.

On Thursday, the central bank chief said the zloty would be devaluated by about nine percent against the basket next year to componsate for high Polish inflation, against a 1996 devaluation of some 12.7 percent.
"Foreigners have not bought anything yet...but one can expect some investment in future," Handlowy's Kowalczyk said.

Overnight rates fell slightly on Friday as banks tried to place surpluss cash for the weekend. Tomorrow/next rates inched up after the central bank offered a one billion zloty reverse repo and a 300 million zloty 273-day NBP-bill sale.
At the 0930 GMT, overnight rates were at 18.95/19.16 percent, down from opening's 19.10/19.30 percent, tomorrow/next were at 19.00/19.24 percent against 18.95/19.20 percent.
Dealers said the large scope of today's drainage may keep rates high for the first part of next week.
